Lessons.Title: Connecting Factors and Zeros
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Identify zeros of polynomial functions written in factored form. Understand that if factors multiplied together equal zero for a specific value of $x$, at least one of the factors must also equal zero at that value of $x$.

A product is zero if any factor is zero. For p(x)=(x-2)(x+3), p(x)=0 at x=2 and -3; these are horizontal intercepts of its graph. Factored form reveals zeros, but a sketch also depends on degree and the leading coefficient.

Source activity 5.1: Notice and Wonder: Factored Form: What do you notice? What do you wonder? \(f(x)=(x+5)(x+1)(x-3)\) \(f(x)=(x+5)(x+1)(x-3)\) \(g(x)=(x+5)(x+1)(x-2)\) \(g(x)=(x+5)(x+1)(x-2)\) \(h(x)=(x+4)(x+1)(x-2)\) \(h(x)=(x+4)(x+1)(x-2)\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 5.2: What Values of $x$ Make These Equations True?: Find all values of \(x\) that make the equation true. \((x+4)(x+2)(x-1)=0\) \((x+4)(x+2)(x-1)(x-3)=0\) \((x+4)^2 (x+2)^2=0\) \(\text-2(x-4)(x-2)(x+1)(x+3)=0\) \((2x+8)(7x-3)(x-10)=0\) \(x(3-x)(x-1)(x+0.75)=0\) Write an equation that is true when \(x\) is equal to -5, 4, or 0 and for no other values of \(x\). Write an equation that is true when \(x\) is equal to -5, 4, or 0 and… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 5.3: Factors, Intercepts, and Graphs: Your teacher will give you a set of cards. Match each equation to either a graph or a description. Take turns with your partner to match an equation with a graph or a description of a graph. For each match that you find, explain to your partner how you know it’s a match. For each match that your partner finds, listen carefully to their explanation. If you disagree, discuss… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
Practice Problem 1: What is the value of \(\displaystyle 4(x-2)(x-3)+7(x-2)(x-5)-6(x-3)(x-5)\) when \(x=5\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Which polynomial function has zeros when \(x=\text-2,\frac34,5\)? \(f(x)=(x-2)(3x+4)(x+5)\) \(f(x)=(x-2)(4x+3)(x+5)\) \(f(x)=(x+2)(3x-4)(x+5)\) \(f(x)=(x+2)(4x-3)(x-5)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: The graph of a polynomial \(f(x)=(2x-3)(x-4)(x+3)\) has \(x\)-intercepts at 3 \(x\) values. What are they? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Match each sequence with one of the recursive definitions. Note that only the part of the definition showing the relationship between the current term and the previous term is given so as not to give away the solutions. One of the sequences matches two recursive definitions. \(a(n) = a(n-1) -4 \) \(b(n) = b(n-1)+0\)… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Han is multiplying \(10x^4\) by \(0.5x^3\) and gets \(5x^7\). He says that \(0.5x^3\) is not a polynomial because 0.5 is not an integer. What is the error in Han’s thinking? Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Here are two expressions whose sum is a new expression, \(A\). \(\displaystyle (2x^2 + 5)+(6x^{\boxed{\phantom{33}}} -7) = A\) Select all the values that we can put in the box so that \(A\) is a polynomial. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Find zeros of 2(x+4)(x-1), and evaluate at x=0. Expected reasoning or answer: Zeros -4 and 1; value -8.
